reason: Public regional art gallery in Bunbury, open to visitors, free; named by Australia's South West and Visit Bunbury Geographe (opened) - two counted sources ('What qualifies' 1-2).
objection: A regional gallery with rotating exhibitions; a 'only if you are nearby' stop for many visitors.

name: Burnside Organic Farm
reason: Organic farm with accommodation and a winery near Margaret River: accommodation/farm business, not a public place to visit ('What qualifies' 2).
objection: Board lists it; farm visits possible only for guests.

name: Bettenay's Margaret River
reason: A shop/bakery/retail venue, not a place to visit ('What qualifies' 2: a venue that is only a shop or restaurant). (Bettenay's is a nougat shop and cellar door.)
objection: Popular family stop for nougat tasting; still a shop/cellar door.

name: A Maze'n Margaret River
reason: Hedge maze and botanical gardens near Margaret River, a permanent paid family attraction for an hour or more ('What qualifies' 2); Australia's South West listing (counted); Wikivoyage Margaret River mentions 'one of the three mazes' without naming it.
objection: Only one counted source names it; a family amusement stop that two other mazes in the area duplicate in kind (Yallingup Maze). Marginal: friend test passes only for families.

name: Golden Valley Tree Park
reason: 60 ha arboretum south of Balingup with 500+ species and walk trails, free and open daily ('What qualifies' 2); Australia's South West and Trails WA (opened) plus Visit Bunbury Geographe and a DBCA guide.
objection: Volunteer-run community arboretum; best in autumn colour, quieter otherwise.

name: Bunbury Museum and Heritage Centre
reason: City museum in the 1886 Bunbury State School, free, open Tue-Sun, Noongar, shipwreck and whaling history ('What qualifies' 2); Australia's South West listing plus the City of Bunbury museum page (opened).
objection: Only one counted visitor source; a modest town museum.

name: Understory Art & Nature Trail
reason: 1.2 km sculpture trail through Northcliffe Forest Park with 70-100 artworks, entered from the Northcliffe Visitor Centre, about an hour ('What qualifies' 2); Australia's South West and Trails WA (opened).
objection: Small paid community trail in a remote village.

name: Manjimup Heritage Park & Power Up Museum
reason: 12 ha heritage park in Manjimup with the State Timber Museum, Age of Steam museum, historical hamlet and fire lookout replica, plus the Power Up electricity museum ('What qualifies' 2); Tourism WA (opened) and Australia's South West.
objection: Partly a town park with playground; museums are small.

name: Yallingup Maze
reason: Large timber maze with towers and bridges plus mini golf on Caves Road, a permanent paid family attraction for an hour or more ('What qualifies' 2); Tourism WA (opened) and Australia's South West - two counted sources.
objection: Family amusement; adults without kids would not go out of their way. Could be review rather than keep.

name: Lake Cave
reason: Show cave with a permanent underground lake and the 'Suspended Table' formation, guided tours daily, near Margaret River ('What qualifies' 1-2); margaretriver.com (opened), Australia's South West, Tourism WA caves page.
objection: None of substance; one of several show caves in the area but a distinct cave.

name: Sugarloaf Rock
reason: Conical granite rock off Cape Naturaliste, a popular sightseeing and sunset stop with car park and Cape to Cape Track access; DBCA Explore Parks site page (opened) and Australia's South West ('What qualifies' 1, 3: a guide names it).
objection: Short stop (15-30 min), on the Cape to Cape Track; but agency singles it out by name.

name: Castle Rock
reason: Outside the region: belongs to wa-great-southern. The Australia's South West listing is Castle Rock and the Granite Skywalk in Porongurup National Park (confirmed by search), not the South West.
objection: The Dunsborough Castle Rock (Meelup) is a different place with no counted source here.

name: Gnomesville
reason: Quirky roadside icon: thousands of garden gnomes at the Wellington Mill roundabout in the Ferguson Valley ('Include: quirky landmarks and roadside icons'); Visit Bunbury Geographe (opened), Tourism WA's Ferguson Valley page and Australia's South West.
objection: Short stop; partly damaged by a November 2024 flood and under restoration.

name: Wyalup-Rocky Point
reason: Basalt headland in Bunbury with 130-million-year-old columnar rock, a beach lookout and interpretive signs, a Noongar significant site ('What qualifies' 2-3); Tourism WA (opened), Visit Bunbury Geographe and Australia's South West. Lies in Bunbury, not Yallingup.
objection: A short stop beside the town beach (Back Beach); 15-30 minutes.

name: Gnarabup Beach
reason: Reef-sheltered swimming and surf beach at Prevelly/Gnarabup, patrolled in summer, with café and coastal trail; margaretriver.com 'Prevelly & Gnarabup' page (opened, Margaret River Busselton Tourism) names Gnarabup Beach. Re-look found a counted source.
objection: Second-tier beach; a near neighbour of Prevelly/Surfers Point if those are listed.

name: Big Brook Dam
reason: Forest dam near Pemberton with a 3.5 km sealed loop walk, beach, picnic areas and Bibbulmun Track access; Tourism WA (opened) and DBCA Explore Parks site page (opened) - two counted sources.
objection: A local recreation reservoir; mostly a picnic/walk stop.

name: Calgardup Bay
reason: No counted source names the bay as a place to go (re-looked: Wikipedia only); its visitor beaches (Gnarabup, Prevelly/Surfers Point, Redgate) are the named stops, so the bay is an umbrella name ('What qualifies' 1, 3).
objection: 216 page views and it does hold popular surf breaks; if listed it would duplicate Gnarabup/Redgate.

name: Torpedo Rocks
reason: Granite outcrops and lookout above Yallingup on the Torpedo Trail (3 km loop) and Cape to Cape Track; Trails WA (opened) names the Torpedo Rock car park and lookout. Re-look found one counted source.
objection: Part of a larger walk (Torpedo Trail / Cape to Cape) and a short lookout; one source; could be folded into Yallingup or the Cape to Cape spot ('What qualifies' 3).

name: Cape Leeuwin Waterwheel
reason: 1895 waterwheel now encrusted in limestone, on the road to Cape Leeuwin Lighthouse; Wikivoyage South West, DBCA Explore Parks 'Water Wheel' site page (opened) and Tourism WA's Cape Leeuwin page all single it out ('What qualifies' 1, 3: a guide names it).
objection: A 10-15 minute stop beside the lighthouse; could be treated as part of Cape Leeuwin.
